# Equal-budget flux when every other fiber is excluded

Use the exact scalar/vector flux conventions of
`candidate 3121a9d11f167d7d`. This note proves
a positive-flux special case and computes the full active trapezoid
circuit. The negative single-cap example cannot be promoted to a negative
active circuit by merely tilting its two other caps to exclude the small
fiber.

## 1. A general isolated-fiber balance lemma

Let `mu` be a finite positive measure on finitely many compact fibers,
with total mass `M`. Fix an anchor `y_*=(z_*,x_*)` in a positive fiber.
Write `g_z` for each full ambient fiber barycenter and `g` for the global
barycenter. Consider finitely many closed caps through the anchor,

    H_j = {a_j.(w-y_*)>=0},  a_j=(v_j,u_j),

having a common mass `D>0`. Suppose every cap has zero measure in every
fiber other than `z_*`. Let `lambda_j>=0`, not all zero, and assume the
RAW continuous normals balance:

    sum_j lambda_j u_j=0.                            (1)

Then the sum of the scalar fluxes satisfies

    sum_j lambda_j J_j >= 0.                         (2)

It is strictly positive if there is any other positive-measure fiber.
The zero outside cap mass assumption is essential to this argument;
merely placing the outside barycenters in the caps' closed complements
does not suffice.

Proof. Let `w_*` be the anchor fiber's mass. Its cap probability is
`D/w_*`, and all other probabilities are zero. The exact flux formula
therefore reduces to

    J_j = D a_j.(g_(z_*)-g).                         (3)

Put `A=sum_j lambda_j a_j`. By (1), `A` has zero continuous component,
so `A.(g_(z_*)-y_*)=0`. In any other positive-measure fiber, every cap
has zero measure, whence `a_j.(w-y_*)<0` almost everywhere in that fiber.
Its expectation is strictly negative. Thus

    A.(g_z-y_*)<0

for every such fiber. Averaging with the positive fiber masses gives
`A.(g-g_(z_*))<0` whenever an outside fiber exists; it gives zero when
none exists. Summing (3) proves the result. No independence of the fiber
laws, monotonic conditional means, or cap-boundary approximation is used.

The raw-normal hypothesis is explicit: center-gradient balance is
`sum_j theta_j S_j u_j=0`, where `S_j` is the coarea section mass. It
implies (1) for `lambda_j=theta_j S_j`, but does not automatically imply
it for `lambda_j=theta_j`.

Here is the contributor's exact reason a barycenter-only replacement would be
false in this finite-measure formulation. At integer indices `0,1`, take
unit-mass continuous measures

    mu_0=(3/4)delta_1+(1/4)delta_(-100),
    mu_1=(1/4)delta_3+(3/4)delta_(-1),

on compact interval fibers containing these supports; the anchor is
`(0,0)`. The caps with margins `L_+=x-z/2` and `L_-=-x-z/2` have equal
mass `1` and opposite continuous normals. The outside barycenter is
`(1,0)`, and both margins there are `-1/2`. Yet the two fluxes are
`J_+=-95/16` and `J_-=-99/16`, whose sum is `-97/8`. These follow directly
from the fiber cap probabilities `(3/4,1/4)` and `(1/4,3/4)`, and scalar
mean pairs `(-97/4,-1/2)` and `(97/4,-1/2)`. Thus the false replacement is
excluded by an exact certificate, not merely by an unavailable proof.

## 2. The exact active trapezoid circuit

Retain the two-fiber example from the identity note, with

    t=(4-sqrt(7))/3,  Delta=t-4/9,
    s=1/t-1,  D=2t-t^2,
    V_0=3/2,  V_1=Delta^2/4,  M=V_0+V_1.

The anchor is `(z,x,y)=(0,0,t)`. The three own-fiber minimum caps have
continuous normals

    u_+=(1,-s),  u_-=(-1,-s),  u_0=(0,1).

Keep these normal scalings fixed in all the following scalar-flux
formulas. For the oblique caps, the coarea section mass is `S_+=S_-=2t`:
their chord runs from height `0` to `2t`, and its Euclidean length divided
by `|u_+|=sqrt(1+s^2)` is `2t`. The upper section has
`S_0=2-t`. Consequently the positive center-gradient balancing weights
are proportional to

    theta_+=theta_-=1,   theta_0=R,
    R=4(1-t)/(2-t).                                  (4)

They can be normalized by dividing all three by `2+R`.

Allow independent integer coefficients `v_+,v_-,v_0`. For every cap to
have total mass exactly `D`, its intersection with the small square
fiber must have zero area. Since that fiber has center
`(0,4/9+Delta/2)` and half-side `Delta/4`, this is equivalent to

    v_0 <= Delta/4,
    v_+,v_- <= -Delta(3s+1)/4.                       (5)

Strict inequalities exclude the entire fiber and make all cap derivatives
transverse. Equality is permitted in the flux computation because its
supporting line has zero area. The scalar fiber-mean differences are

    delta m_0 = v_0+Delta/2 <= 3Delta/4,
    delta m_+,delta m_- = v_+,v_- - sDelta/2
                       <= -Delta(5s+1)/4.

Formula (3), or direct two-fiber summation, gives

    J_j = -(D V_1/M) delta m_j.

Thus for the UNNORMALIZED weights in (4), every admissible integer tilt
obeys the exact strictly positive lower bound

    J_+ + J_- + R J_0
      >= (D V_1 Delta/(4M)) [2(5s+1)-3R] > 0.        (6)

Indeed

    2(5s+1)-3R
      = [20t^2-38t+20]/[t(2-t)] > 0,

since the numerator is `2(10t^2-19t+10)`, whose discriminant is
`19^2-4*10*10=-39`. All other factors are strictly positive. Divide
(6) by `2+R` for normalized center-gradient weights.

For an especially simple strict choice take

    v_0=0,   v_+=v_-=-s Delta.

The side-fiber maximum cap margin is `Delta(1-s)/4<0`, since `s>1`.
Writing `C_0=D V_1 Delta/(2M)>0`, the individual fluxes are exactly

    J_0=-C_0,   J_+=J_-=3s C_0,

and the center-gradient weighted sum is

    C_0(6s-R)>0.                                    (7)

For raw-normal weights `(1,1,2s)`, the sum is `4s C_0>0`, consistent
with Section 1. This verifies explicitly why the negative horizontal
active cap alone does not obstruct the relevant full circuit budget.

## 3. Scope of the surviving obstruction

The root's separate symmetric three-fiber construction has a negative
flux for an equal-budget active opposite pair; it is not covered by
Section 1 because both endpoint fibers contribute to both caps. Its
certificate is `candidate ae6d727221cffaef` and has
passed an independent line-by-line audit here. Therefore
equal budgets, full section-centroid stationarity, and coarea-gradient
balance still do not imply a nonnegative global flux in general.

All examples so far have depth greater than the OC target. The combined
results neither establish nor refute a signed-flux inequality under an
actual below-target cap budget at a minimizing convex body.
